data.narrative:
Radian Forge is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $3M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private robotics and manufacturing firms and 1 public comparable, though the private peer set lacks sufficient narrow-stage cohesion for reliable median-based pricing.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach, using total capital raised ($3M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $8M. The Peer-Median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics sector; while 8 private peers exist in the broader sector, filtering for Seed-stage or similar-tier companies produces fewer than 3 datapoints required for reliable median benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M (low) to $9M (high), with a median of $8M. This range reflects the single-method triangulation with a ±15% band around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the lack of robust peer pricing at Seed stage in this subsector, limiting downside/upside calibration, and the quality of total-raised-as-proxy in capturing true post-money economics. Additional disclosure of actual post-money valuation from the most recent round, or comparable exits in the robotics subsector, would narrow this range materially.
